data.name: Eshwar
data.gender_notes: Eshwar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Eshwar is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Ishvara’ which means ‘Lord of the Universe’. In Hinduism, Ishvara is the supreme god, the ruler of all creation. Eshwar is a revered name for boys, symbolizing power, authority, and devotion to the divine. The name Eshwar carries the meaning “Lord of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Eshwar usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of devotion and connection to the divine
data.etymology: Eshwar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Eshwar total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eshwar carries deep cultural roots and symbolizes the devotion and faith of Hindus towards their revered god, Ishvara. It is a name that resonates with a sense of power, authority, and godliness. The name is used not only to address the divine deity but also to honor and bestow respect upon respected elders and authorities.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Eshwar holds immense spiritual significance as it refers to the supreme deity, Ishvara. This name reminds us of the divine presence that is omnipresent and omnipotent, guiding and protecting us through our lives. Eshwar is a name that inspires devotion, surrender, and a deep connection to the divine. It is a reminder of the belief that ultimately, all power and control lies with the divine, as we are but a small part of the vast cosmic order.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Eshwar signifies the supreme god, the ruler of the universe. It symbolizes the infinite, omnipotent, and omniscient power that governs all creation. In Hinduism, Eshwar embodies the essence of absolute consciousness, love, and compassion.

vedic_reference.note: Eshwar is a common name in Hinduism and is associated with various Hindu deities, particularly Shiva and Vishnu.
